findings.statement: A restart's new plan can make a former accessory the vertical MAIN. restartProgram builds a new plan, so the plane rule asks as in any new plan and heldAs sees only earlier sessions of the new week (D-14). In 46 of 780 restarts, all 4 strength days to 2 (1- or 6-week pause), the asking MAIN slot takes a configuration the plan before held only as ACCESSORY (lat-pulldown, db-overhead-press, barbell-overhead-press, pike-push-up) where the same restart without the plane rule takes the horizontal default. The MAIN row is re-established at the MAIN dose (no accessory dose state reaches it): 0 of 46 loaded MAIN rows outside the goal range through nine weeks, set and repetition trails mirror the slot without the rule. New-plan output is byte-identical on 76b8448 and 5f7f6f6, so this is not changed by the fix. Whether a restart may promote a former accessory into the vertical MAIN slot is a sporting reading for the SSCTR (criterion 2 is stated for plans in force).

The declared cost of D-18, measured: after a change of days that changes the templates the plan stops alternating, permanently and silently. With the predecessor's r2-b, 88 of 308 sequences lose a vertical the plan held as MAIN (was 2): 2->4 9, 4->2 28, 3->4 14, 4->3 14, 2->5 9, 5->2 14; none in 2<->3. No slot asks again afterwards, also after a return to the original days (2->4->2), because the anchors are gone. Deterministic, pinned by the new tests, equal to the engine without the rule, no dose consequence; no athlete-facing text claims plane coverage and none discloses the end of alternation. No quality reason against; acceptability is the SSCTR's, disclosure is an integration matter.
